title: Algebraic theory of abelian fractons and beyond
authors: Wilbur Shirley, Evan Wickenden, Bowen Yang, Agnès Beaudry, Michael Hermele
abstract: We develop an algebraic theory of fusion, mobility, and statistics in abelian gapped fracton orders and topological phases. The framework generalizes the algebraic description of abelian anyons to systems with restricted-mobility and spatially extended excitations. We consider translation-invariant bosonic systems whose pointlike and extended excitations have finite fusion order. The basic objects are braided fusion complexes (BFCs): chain complexes encoding fusion and mobility, equipped with a braiding chain map encoding statistics. Their equivalence classes define braided fusion theories (BFTs). Our framework encompasses arbitrary translation-invariant Pauli codes, as well as all abelian anyon theories in two spatial dimensions, including chiral theories. We give evidence for the conjecture that every nondegenerate BFT can be realized as the excitation theory of a gapped phase and that the BFT describing such a phase is a phase invariant. We derive constraints on pointlike fusion and mobility, showing, for example, that neither the Pauli X nor Z sectors of the X-cube and anisotropic models can occur alone in a nondegenerate BFT. For nondegenerate theories with only pointlike excitations, we extract a simpler theory of mutual statistics, consisting of a fusion module and a map to its statistical dual. This theory of mutual statistics is an invariant of the BFT and, at odd fusion order, gives an equivalent description of the full braided fusion theory. We interpret remote detection as the generalization of mutual statistics to fracton orders. In the BFC setting, we give a precise formulation of the excitation-detector principle: every nontrivial excitation can be detected by an operator supported at spatial infinity, and every nontrivial detector detects some excitation. Assuming a unique infinite-space ground state, we prove that this principle is equivalent to nondegeneracy.
summary: This paper develops a novel algebraic theory using Braided Fusion Complexes (BFCs) to classify topological phases characterized by abelian fracton excitations. It generalizes existing anyon theories by incorporating excitation mobility and establishes that the algebraic nondegeneracy of the theory is equivalent to the physical existence of a gapped phase. This provides a powerful invariant for characterizing exotic quantum matter states.
main_problem: To develop a comprehensive algebraic theory describing fusion, mobility, and statistics for excitations in gapped topological phases, particularly those exhibiting restricted mobility (fractons).
main_result: The authors introduce Braided Fusion Complexes (BFCs) and Braided Fusion Theories (BFTs) as the fundamental invariants, establishing that nondegeneracy of the BFT is equivalent to the phase being a gapped abelian phase.
method: The theory employs advanced algebraic structures, specifically chain complexes, to encode fusion (via quasi-isomorphism types) and statistics (via a braiding chain map).
model_or_system: The theory applies to translation-invariant bosonic systems, encompassing abelian anyon theories in 2D, arbitrary Pauli codes, and general abelian fracton orders.
key_observables: Braided Fusion Complexes (BFCs), Braided Fusion Theories (BFTs), Mutual Statistics, and the Excitation-Detector Principle.
important_parameters: Finite fusion order, dimensionality (d), and the nondegeneracy condition.
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to be bosonic, translation-invariant, and possess a unique infinite-space ground state for the equivalence proofs.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the basic algebraic objects (BFCs) to generalizing the theory beyond standard anyons to include mobility (fractons). It then derives constraints on these theories and proves the equivalence between nondegeneracy and the physical realization of the phase.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework to classify topological phases based on their excitation statistics, which is crucial for understanding exotic quantum matter states beyond simple 2D anyons.
